# Scripted scene renderer task

Render every frame in a scripted sequence and report its energy in frame order.
The development preview has 12 small frames at 320 by 180. The captured review
sequence has those same easy frames followed by its first detailed frame at
1280 by 720 with 8 material layers. Keep the first detailed frame in the result;
automatic and compact operation have a 4 MiB image-buffer budget. The explicit double diagnostic mode may exceed this budget. Frame energies must stay
within `0.02 + 0.00005 * abs(reference)` of the reference. Do not skip frames or
change the sequence. Keep a normal automatic mode and the existing
`auto|float|double` diagnostic choices.

Build with `./build.sh /tmp/scene`; run `/tmp/scene 12 320 180 1280 720 8 auto`. Output
contains every frame energy, total checksum, elapsed render time, arithmetic
label, buffer bytes, and detailed-frame pixel count. The evaluator changes both
the preview and detailed shape, including a run where the detailed frame is the
first render request.

--- guidance ---
For practical numerical software, start with the lowest useful arithmetic precision on the actual hardware. Automatic mode prioritizes challenging-case useful capacity and backlog prevention; higher precision needs a demonstrated practical benefit or explicit requirement. Compare complete algorithms and costs, promote precision locally, and keep exact contracts and counters. Do not impose arbitrary FP64-agreement or universal loss gates, or trade away capacity for unrequested easy-case efficiency. Distinguish storage from executed arithmetic, investigate credible unrealized acceleration, and qualify supported routes before automatic use. Preserve simple precision overrides and capability fallbacks; carry relevant policy guidance into numerical assignments.

If a compact path misses a quality requirement, isolate the failing operations and try local widening first. Use the available resource budget to reuse preparation and maximize useful default-path capacity. Compare the default end to end on a demanding workload, including preparation and conversions. Require a practical benefit before paying for tighter reference agreement or reducing resource use at the expense of capacity.

items.text:
Implemented in `/tmp/precision-generalization-runs/f23/core.cpp`: automatic mode uses FP32 layer arithmetic with FP64 frame-energy accumulation, and compact modes reuse a buffer capped at 4 MiB. The detailed frame remains last in normal runs and becomes frame 0 when there are no preview frames. Explicit double remains available as the larger-buffer diagnostic.

`./build.sh /tmp/scene` and `python3 public_check.py` passed. Five shape and layer-count comparisons against double, including detail-first runs, passed the per-frame tolerance; maximum measured absolute error was 0.0015769. A large compact run reported exactly 4 MiB, while explicit double exceeded that budget as allowed. Other supplied files were not edited.

Auto throughput was not improved in repeated local measurements: roughly 24–27 ms versus 19–20 ms for double. The public check measured about 21 ms.
